confirmedFindings.finding: W2-A established canonical Batch/InventoryPosition identities, exact integer quantities, immutable availability snapshots and PostgreSQL RESERVE/RELEASE under a memberless command owner.

W2-B requires every new Auction lot to bind one canonical Inventory reservation atomically. The bound lot is DECLARED and PUBLIC_ALLOWED with source_verified_at kept null; the legacy verified-lot command is denied.

The existing canonical Deal repository consumes one confirmed auction DEAL_BASIS_READY event and atomically creates Deal, participants, event, audit and outbox receipt, but it does not yet consume or normalize the Auction inventory binding.

Auction close derives the exact winning bid and emits the canonical Deal basis. That basis currently carries commercial terms only; inventory allocation must be server-derived from the already-bound lot rather than added as browser input.

implementedBoundaries.result: Canonical inventory position/reservation authority, exact quantities, concurrent capacity protection, durable receipts/snapshots/audit/outbox and restricted-principal restore acceptance.

Existing Auction registration consumes canonical Inventory reservation atomically; exact commodity/profile/quantity binding is immutable; DECLARED + PUBLIC_ALLOWED is separated from independent verification; bound reservations cannot be released/reused through the old lifecycle.

sourceAnchorDelta: W2-B is merged and accepted in #5040. New Auction lots are inventory-bound and declared-public without fabricated verification. The remaining immediate gap is the existing canonical Deal creation edge: PrismaDealRepository validates Auction basis but does not yet allocate the winning quantity against the immutable inventory binding.

nextContinuation.name: Canonical Deal inventory allocation from the existing Auction award
acceptance: One existing PrismaDealRepository transaction creates the canonical Deal and one exact inventory allocation linked to the same lot binding, winning bid and award; no parallel Deal or stock engine.
Winning quantity is server-derived from the awarded bid and pinned Inventory profile/unit identity. Client stock/verification fields are not accepted as authority.
Partial winning quantity allocates only the winner's exact quantity and conserves the unallocated remainder without falsely committing, shipping, accepting or selling it.
Revoked seller/buyer authority cannot obtain a replayed success. Missing allocation, audit, outbox, award or actor evidence rolls back the Deal creation completely.
Runtime/seed/SET ROLE/legacy definer paths cannot insert an application Deal without the required inventory allocation; historical privileged migration fixtures remain explicitly isolated.
RLS overlay, one-deal reset and DR restore preserve the bound-reservation guard and stock conservation.
